I am 73 years old this year. I went to primary school for a few years when I was young, then I came back to the field and have been farming for 50 years now. My family has 13.1 mu of land. Most of it — about 8 mu — I plant wheat in winter and then maize right after the wheat comes off. The other 5.1 mu I keep for cotton. That is what I have been doing for many years, and I know how to handle it.

For wheat, I will sow Jimai 22. I buy 30 jin of seed per mu — that is about 15 kg. My neighbor Old Wang had good luck with this variety last year, so I am sticking with it. Before sowing around October 10th, I run the rotary tiller over the field. For fertilizer, I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu — about 50 kg of that 28-6-6 compound as basal, and then at green-up time I topdress with another 25 kg of urea. In total, that comes to about 38 kg of nitrogen per mu, 18 kg of phosphorus, and 6 kg of potassium. I irrigate three times: once before winter freeze, once at jointing, and once at heading. The well pump costs money, so I do not waste water, but three times is what this land needs. For sprays, I do herbicide once after sowing, insecticide twice when the aphids come, and fungicide once if I see rust. I expect about 1000 jin per mu, which is 500 kg.

For maize, I plant Denghai 605 hybrid seed. I use one small package per mu, about 1.2 kg. I do not till again after wheat — I just plant directly into the stubble with the no-till planter right after wheat harvest around June 10th. I put down 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, and then side-dress with urea when the plants are knee-high. That gives about 32 kg nitrogen, 12 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium per mu. Maize does not need as much water as wheat — I irrigate twice, once at the big喇叭口 stage and once at tasseling. For chemicals, I spray herbicide once and insecticide twice for the corn borer. I expect about 1100 jin per mu, which is 550 kg.

For cotton on my 5.1 mu, I use Guoxinmian seed. I sow about 3 jin per mu, which is 1.5 kg. I rotary till the cotton plot in spring because cotton likes loose soil. I put down 50 kg of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, and topdress once with urea at flowering. That is about 25 kg nitrogen, 10 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium per mu. Cotton needs water but not too much — I irrigate twice, at budding and at flowering. But cotton needs a lot of spraying. The bollworm is the worst pest. I spray insecticide 12 times through the season, plus herbicide once and fungicide once. That is 14 sprayings total. It costs money, but if the bollworm gets bad, the whole crop is finished. I expect about 550 jin of seed cotton per mu, which is 275 kg.

I think carefully about costs. My son and daughter-in-law work in the county town and send some money home, so I have a little cushion. But fertilizer and pesticide prices have gone up. I would rather put a bit more fertilizer than lose yield — a bad harvest means no money for my grandson's school fees. Last year I did about the same rates and things were fine. Old Wang across the lane does similar amounts, and his crops always look good. So I will do what I did before, with only small adjustments.
